title: Era of Cyrus: Persian power begins
summary: CFAH AP-7: the beginning of the Persian power under Cyrus II (560/559 BC); in Herodotus, Astyages loses the Median crown to Cyrus after 35 years (1.130).
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Sorted by the CFAH anchor point cited below; Herodotus entries are display only.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 3: Anchor Points of Ancient History," ARJ 16 (2023): 131–154, section "AP-7: Era of Cyrus (Persian Empire): 560/559 B.C."
chronologies.note: CFAH-3: "The Persian Empire ended in 330 B.C., thus 230 years yields 560/559 B.C. for the beginning of the Persian power." CFAH-5 (AP-32) adds that Herodotus appears to have counted his Median reigns to "the accession of Cyrus as coregent with his father in 560 B.C."

chronologies.date: “after a reign of thirty-five years, Astyages lost his crown”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.130 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 60 (PDF p. 62)
chronologies.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 595/594 BC − 35 = 560/559 BC, the CFAH Era of Cyrus (AP-7). Total Deioces→Astyages' fall = 53 + 22 + 40 + 35 = 150 years (CFAH-5 makes the same sum). Agrees with CFAH AP-7 (560/559 BC). Generations (provisional) dates Cyrus's founding of the Medo-Persian empire to 550 BC, 10 years later; CFAH-5 explains this as Herodotus counting to Cyrus's coregency (560) and Ctesias to the defeat of Astyages (550).

chronologies.date: “Cyrus himself fell, after reigning nine and twenty years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.214 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 94 (PDF p. 96)
chronologies.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): CFAH AP-7 (560/559 BC) − 29 = 531/530 BC for the death of Cyrus. CFAH-3 (AP-8) counts Cyrus 30 years (560 − 30 = 530 for Cambyses' accession), one year more than Herodotus. Generations prints Cyrus 600–530 BC (provisional), 0–1 year from the derived death.
